titleEn: Eat a Bit of Everything—Swim Fast!

pages.text: "Only bread! I don't like greens!" Mumu the little brother pushed greens and carrots to the edge of his plate. He picked only bread to eat. Beside him, big sister Dodo happily ate a bit of everything.
"Tomorrow I'll swim faster than you!" Mumu said, munching bread. Green and orange food stayed at the plate edge. Mom from the mill looked at it quietly.
The next morning, in the stream, Dodo's webbed feet paddled her swiftly ahead. Mumu wobbled behind. His feet felt heavy. "I paddle and paddle, but I don't move!"
Mom sat on the bank and called him. "Mumu, you ate only bread yesterday, right? You're missing green strength and orange strength." His beak opened wide. "Green strength?"
Mom whispered, "Green is foot strength, orange is wing strength. Eat a bit of everything to swim fast." Ahead, Dodo cut swiftly through the water. Really? Mumu watched her wake.
That evening, Mom put green leaves, orange carrots, and bread on the plate and sang, "Eat a bit of everything—swim fast!" Mumu stared at the plate. Dodo was already crunching.
Mumu broke a piece of orange carrot with his beak. Crunch! "...Oh? It's sweet!" The greens crunched too. He picked up another bite. "Eat a bit of everything—swim fast!"
The next morning, in the stream—oh? His webbed feet felt light as feathers. Mumu paddled fast, right beside Dodo! One flick of his tail. Dodo grinned.
Now Mumu knew the rule. "One, a bite of green leaves! Two, a bite of orange carrot! Three, a bite of bread too!" At dinner, he pointed a wingtip at his first helping. "Green first!"
Mom hugged Mumu warmly on the bank. "Eating everything made you fast, right?" A bit of everything helps strength grow. Splash! Mumu swam, calling, "Eat a bit of everything—swim fast!"
